properties.description: On April 7, 2025, the City of Seattle Department of Construction & Inspections (SDCI) Code Compliance Division cited the Applicant with a Shoreline Violation (Record Number 1060659-VI) for a series of unauthorized exterior developments conducted within the steep-slope hazardous area and shoreline jurisdiction (the shoreline jurisdiction encompasses the entire subject property) associated with Elliott Bay (Puget Sound). The cited unauthorized developments included installation of a new staircase, modifications to the bulkhead and the area landward of the bulkhead, excavation at the toe of the slope, vegetation removal, and placement of cement (impervious) surfaces behind the bulkhead. However, several components of the unauthorized development are expected to be considered repair or maintenance of existing structures, as the previously existing features were no longer safe for continued use and were replaced within their original development footprints. These elements include the replacement wooden staircase along the southern western portion of the subject property and the replacement of the landscaping wall located landward of the bulkhead. Additionally, based on the geotechnical assessment provided by Migizi Group, Inc. (MGI), the completed unauthorized work has not adversely affected slope stability or contributed to slope erosion at the subject property. Accordingly, the Applicant is pursuing after-the-fact authorization through the shoreline variance permitting pathway for the completed work within the shoreline jurisdiction. The Applicant remains committed to ensuring that the overall project results in no net loss of shoreline ecological function compared to pre-project conditions and anticipates that the proposed actions will achieve a net gain in shoreline ecological function.

The cited unauthorized developments included installation of a new staircase, modifications to the bulkhead and the area landward of the bulkhead, excavation at the toe of the slope, vegetation removal, and placement of cement (impervious) surfaces behind the bulkhead. However, several components of the unauthorized development are expected to be considered repair or maintenance of existing structures, as the previously existing features were no longer safe for continued use and were replaced within their original development footprints. These elements include the replacement wooden staircase along the southern western portion of the subject property and the replacement of the landscaping wall located landward of the bulkhead. Additionally, based on the geotechnical assessment provided by Migizi Group, Inc. (MGI), the completed unauthorized work has not adversely affected slope stability or contributed to slope erosion at the subject property. Accordingly, the Applicant is pursuing after-the-fact authorization through the shoreline variance permitting pathway for the completed work within the shoreline jurisdiction. The Applicant remains committed to ensuring that the overall project results in no net loss of shoreline ecological function compared to pre-project conditions and anticipates that the proposed actions will achieve a net gain in shoreline ecological function.

properties.description:
The proposed Pier 1 demolition and replacement activities include:

(1)Demolition of the existing Pier 1 timber and concrete structure.
(2)Installation of a commercial grade pier and an adjacent marina facility within the previous pier footprint. Activity is anticipated to include installation of a sheet pile wall within a portion of the aquatic habitat below the existing pier. Filling activities will occur behind the sheet pile wall to support installation of the new pier and marina facility.
(3)

Restoration of the existing shoreline revetment adjacent to the new pier and marina.
(4)Shoreline excavation to create area of gravel beach to compensate for unavoidable aquatic habitat impacts.






The existing pier consists of approximately 1,900 creosote piles and is significantly deteriorated with only a perimeter concrete apron that is in any measure of serviceable use. Replacement of the pier is needed to maintain the industrial/commercial marine use of the pier.

Based on soil and groundwater investigations, it is reported that upland soil, composed predominately of fill materials, is contaminated with metals and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs).

Restoration of the existing shoreline revetment is needed to prevent further erosion of the shoreline, and will assist in containing contaminated upland soils onsite.

Fill activities proposed below a portion of the existing pier's footprint, will partially utilize upland contaminated soils and suspected contaminated sediment (to the extent practicable) that will be disturbed during the course of  pier demolition and replacement activities and shoreline restoration. A sheet pile wall is proposed waterward of the area of fill to provide containment of the upland soil and dewatered sediment and protect the new pier structure. The new retaining wall feature will be contiguous with adjacent proposed shoreline revetment.
